metadata.goal: Analyze how vessels organize and adjust their movements within a broad bidirectional traffic flow.
metadata.dataset_description: Constructed northbound and southbound traffic in an established offshore corridor west of Jutland, with stable passages and short manoeuvring phases.
metadata.source_note: Danish maritime geography is used as context; the visible trajectories and attributes are constructed derived data.

insight_list.insight: Northbound and southbound traffic forms two laterally offset movement bands, with northbound vessels concentrated farther west.

plot.title: Bidirectional Traffic Bands
plot.description: Compare the lateral positions of northbound and southbound trajectories in the same corridor.

insight_list.question: How are the two directional flows organized laterally?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the lateral positions of northbound and southbound trajectories in the same corridor.

insight_list.insight: Most vessels maintain stable COG and lateral position for long periods, interrupted by short manoeuvring phases with lower speed and greater directional variation before stable navigation resumes.

plot.title: Stable Navigation and Short Manoeuvres
plot.description: Compare speed, COG variation, and lateral position inside and outside short manoeuvring phases.

insight_list.question: How are stable periods interrupted by short manoeuvring phases?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare speed, COG variation, and lateral position inside and outside short manoeuvring phases.

insight_list.insight: Lower-speed passages show greater lateral dispersion within both directional flows, while faster passages remain more tightly concentrated within their dominant movement bands.

plot.title: Speed and Lateral Dispersion
plot.description: Compare continuous passage speed with within-band lateral dispersion separately for both directions.

insight_list.question: How is passage speed associated with lateral dispersion?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare continuous passage speed with within-band lateral dispersion separately for both directions.

insights: Northbound and southbound traffic forms two laterally offset movement bands, with northbound vessels concentrated farther west.
Most vessels maintain stable COG and lateral position for long periods, interrupted by short manoeuvring phases with lower speed and greater directional variation before stable navigation resumes.
Lower-speed passages show greater lateral dispersion within both directional flows, while faster passages remain more tightly concentrated within their dominant movement bands.
summary: Northbound and southbound traffic forms two laterally offset movement bands, with northbound vessels concentrated farther west. Most vessels maintain stable COG and lateral position for long periods, interrupted by short manoeuvring phases with lower speed and greater directional variation before stable navigation resumes. Lower-speed passages show greater lateral dispersion within both directional flows, while faster passages remain more tightly concentrated within their dominant movement bands.
